newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey ends aircraft bids' assessment - officials.
newsitem.headline: Turkey ends aircraft bids' assessment - officials.

text.p: Turkey has completed the assessment of aircraft production proposals made by McDonnell Douglas Corp, Boeing Co and Airbus Industrie, officials from the prime minister's office said on Tuesday.
They said the evaluated bids were expected to be presented to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan this week before the announcement of the tender results.
Turkey has sought the bids to meet the demand of national carrier Turkish Airlines for 54 passenger aircraft.
Turkish officials say the three companies have accepted Turkey's proposal that the aircraft be produced under a 50 percent offset agreement.
Under such an agreement, 50 percent of the sum paid for the aircraft is awarded to domestic industry in the form of contracts.

The planned agreement envisages the manufacture of 34 planes in a first batch, followed by a second batch of 20 aircraft, the officials said. They said deliveries could begin next year if orders are presented this year.
